profiles.final_question: For each of the three base policies, what road ambulance cover is provided and what conditions or limits apply? No optional covers are selected.

source_answer.text: Family Health Optima Insurance Plan: Road ambulance expenses are payable up to INR 750 per hospitalization and INR 1,500 per policy period, subject to an admissible hospitalization claim. Covered transport includes a private ambulance when medically needed to reach hospital, hospital-to-hospital transfer for a higher level of medical treatment, or transport home in the same city when ambulance use is certified by a medical practitioner. The hospitalization claim must be admissible. Transport home must be within the same city and ambulance use must be certified by a medical practitioner.

source_answer.text: Star Comprehensive Insurance Policy: Road ambulance expenses cover medically needed private-ambulance transport to a hospital, private-ambulance transfer between hospitals for further medical treatment, and transport from the treating hospital to the insured person’s residence in the same city. The road ambulance expense is payable subject to an admissible hospitalization claim. Transport from the treating hospital to the residence must be within the same city, and a medical practitioner must certify the need for an ambulance.

profiles.final_question: For each of the three base policies, what AYUSH inpatient treatment is covered, and what hospital, treatment and payment conditions apply? No optional covers are selected. City and premium budget remain unknown.

source_answer.text: Family Health Optima Insurance Plan: AYUSH inpatient hospitalization expenses for treatment under Ayurveda, Unani, Siddha and Homeopathy are payable up to the Sum Insured in an AYUSH Hospital. Yoga and Naturopathy claims require prior company approval. An AYUSH Hospital may be a government AYUSH hospital, a recognized teaching hospital, or a registered standalone/co-located inpatient facility supervised by a qualified registered AYUSH practitioner and meeting the stated facility criteria. Treatment must occur as inpatient hospitalization in an AYUSH Hospital. Yoga and Naturopathy claims require prior company approval. A standalone or co-located AYUSH hospital must be registered where applicable and supervised by a qualified registered AYUSH practitioner. That facility must have at least 5 inpatient beds, a qualified AYUSH practitioner in charge around the clock, required therapy sections or an equipped operation theatre, and accessible daily patient records.

profiles.final_question: For each of the three base policies, what organ-donor expenses are covered, and what conditions, limits and exclusions apply? No optional covers are selected.

source_answer.text: Family Health Optima Insurance Plan: Organ-donor expenses are covered for organ transplantation where the insured person is the recipient. The transplantation claim must be payable, and cover is subject to available Sum Insured. Donor screening expenses and the donor's post-donation complications are excluded. The limit is 10% of the Sum Insured or INR 100,000, whichever is less. The insured person must be the organ recipient. The transplantation claim must be payable and sufficient Sum Insured must remain available. Donor screening expenses and post-donation complications of the donor are not payable.

citations.quote:
Organ Donor Expenses for organ
transplantation where the Insured Person
is the recipient are payable provided
the claim for transplantation is payable
and subject to the availability of the
Sum Insured.

Donor screening expenses
and post-donation complications of
the donor are not payable.

This cover is
subject to a limit of 10% of the Sum Insured
or Rupees One lakh, whichever is less.

source_answer.text: Star Comprehensive Insurance Policy: Covers the donor’s inpatient hospitalization expenses for organ transplantation to the insured recipient when the transplantation claim is payable. Donor expenses for complications requiring redo surgery or ICU admission are also covered. The limit is additional to the Limit of Coverage, up to the Basic Sum Insured, and may be used only by the donor. A 10% co-payment applies under Section II.9 when entry age is 61 years or above, except where entry occurred before age 61 and renewal continued without a break. The transplant must satisfy the Transplantation of Human Organs Act of 1994 and amendments. Treatment must be in India. The transplantation claim must be payable. The additional limit may be used by the donor, not the insured. The stated co-payment applies to Section II.9, subject to the continuous-renewal exception.

source_answer.text: Family Health Optima Insurance Plan: Retrieved evidence incomplete: coverage: coverage_question: The supplied bounded packet does not establish whether consumables or non-medical expenses are covered during an admissible inpatient or day-care claim. It only states that pharmacy and consumables are excluded from “Associated Medical Expenses” and are not subject to proportionate deduction; this does not itself establish payment coverage or provide the covered-item list and exclusions. needs_prospectus: relevant coverage wording or consumables/non-medical-expenses schedule is required.

Star Comprehensive Insurance Policy: Retrieved evidence incomplete: coverage: coverage_question: The supplied bounded packet does not contain an explicit base-policy benefit, exclusion, or covered-item list establishing whether consumables or non-medical expenses are payable during an admissible inpatient or day-care claim. The wording only states that pharmacy, consumables, implants, medical devices, diagnostics and ICU charges are outside “Associated Medical Expenses” for proportionate-deduction purposes; that does not establish coverage or non-coverage. Omitted pages cannot support an absence inference. needs_prospectus: complete relevant benefit and exclusion provisions are required.

Star Health Assure Insurance Policy: The base policy covers the non-medical items (consumables) identified in List I when there is an admissible inpatient or day-care claim. The supplied packet does not reproduce List I, so the individual covered items cannot be enumerated here. Dietary supplements and non-prescription substances are excluded unless prescribed by a medical practitioner as part of a hospitalization claim or day-care procedure. No optional cover is required for this stated base coverage. The underlying inpatient or day-care claim must be admissible. Only items listed in policy List I become payable. Dietary supplements and substances purchasable without prescription are excluded unless prescribed by a medical practitioner as part of a hospitalization claim or day-care procedure.
